To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interference power level and the CIR between 60-GHz and 2.4-GHz on-body radio links can be characterized using a normal distribution and that the interference power is lower and the CIR higher at 60 GHz compared to 2,45 GHz.
interference levels and CIRs at 60 GHz are significantly lower than at 2.4 GHz for both omnidirectional and directional antennas.
60-GHz on-body radio transmissions are less prone to interference than 2.45-GHz transmissions and that directional antennas can be adopted to further mitigate interference.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interuser interference between adjacent wireless body area networks (WBANs) worn by two persons in an indoor office environment at 60 GHz.
the interuser interference between two wireless body area networks in a shared environment.
the interuser interference between two adjacent wireless body area networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
60 GHz provides a significant advantage in reducing interuser interference between two adjacent wireless body area networks compared to 2,45 GHz.

the use of 60 GHz in WBANs would be beneficial for reducing the interference power-level and increasing the CIR compared to the use of 2.45GHz, both with omnidi- and directional antennas, in indoor environments.
, in general, the use of 60 GHz is beneficial in reducing the interference between on-body wireless devices worn by two moving users in an indoor environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 60-GHz band provides an excellent opportunity for wireless body area networks in terms of interference reduction.

the interference power level at 60 GHz is reduced by approximately 20 dB compared to 2-45 GHz, which results in an approximately 30 dB improvement in the instantaneous carrier-to-interference-ratio (CIR).
60-GHz on-body communications can be a promising candidate for body-centric networks, especially when the body is moving.
The main takeaway from our work is that
60-GHz on-body communications offer significantly lower levels of interuser interference than 2.45-GHz communications in an indoor environment.
interference levels can be significantly reduced at 60 GHz using on-body antennas, both omnidirectional and directional.
the use of directional antennas at 60 GHz is an effective way of reducing interuser interference in wireless body area networks.
